group.description:
Virtual Innovative Research & Technology (VIRaTeC) is a global academic and industry community  connecting students, educators, researchers, and innovators through AI, EdTech, and international collaboration.
We create inclusive virtual environments where participants from different countries work together on joint projects, discussions, and problem-solving tasks using modern communication technologies. This approach makes global learning more accessible while promoting intercultural competence, digital literacy, critical thinking, and subject-specific expertise.

The philosophy behind the VIRaTeC Global Community:
We do not educate students to fit into a predetermined future. We create opportunities for them to discover themselves, explore their potential, create their own futures, and take responsibility for shaping the world in which they will live and work.
A distinctive feature of VIRaTeC is our Certified  Research-Based Learning model. Master’s students, guided by the International Board of Advisors, present and facilitate thematic workshops for international cohorts of UGs  within the field of Information Technologies. Through these activities, young researchers gain valuable opportunities to share their knowledge and expertise with peers worldwide. As the result, all the participants are granted by the  Certificates of Completion / Distinction / Acknowledgement. 
Working in diverse international teams enables students to strengthen both hard and soft skills while developing competencies in:
• Project Design  
• Project Management  
• Team Leadership  
• Moderation and Facilitation  
• Data Analysis and Research  
• Workshop Coaching and Digital Collaboration
VIRaTeC supports the development of globally minded professionals capable of collaborating effectively across cultures, disciplines, and technological domains.

posts.summary: Students from six named countries participated in an offshore wind farm negotiation role-play. The post identifies Dr. Kelly Tzoumis of Johns Hopkins University as the initiator.

🌊 Learning Through Experience!
 🇺🇸🇺🇦🇲🇦 🇨🇲 🇯🇴🇩🇿

Yesterday, I had the privilege of observing how students from the USA 🇺🇸, Ukraine 🇺🇦, Morocco 🇲🇦, Cameroon 🇨🇲, Jordan 🇯🇴, and Algeria 🇩🇿 were actively engaged in an offshore wind farm negotiation, representing different roles and interests. 

What began as an immersive role-play initiated by Dr. Kelly Tzoumis, Principal Investigator at Johns Hopkins University 🇺🇸quickly became a powerful lesson in communication, collaboration, and personal growth.

The master’s students faced a complex, real-world challenge together. As they negotiated across national, religious, and identity-related differences, they were not only developing solutions; they were also learning to listen, lead, adapt, and contribute from perspectives different from their own. 

The carefully structured educational environment of the role-play enabled students to step beyond their comfort zones, experience complexity, collaborate across borders, and discover what they were capable of.
My main TakeAway: sometimes, the most important learning is not about the problem itself, but it is about who we become while solving it.

posts.summary: The post describes an asynchronous project combining gerontology and data analytics from March 9 to April 18. It names KNU, Pryazovskyi State Technical University and Georgia State University, Perimeter College.
posts.full_text:
🌍 VIRaTeC COIL | Global Virtual Exchange Experience within an Interdisciplinary COIL Project hosted by Georgia State University (🇺🇸)

📍 This initiative brought together first-year undergraduate students majoring in Computer Science from the Faculty of Information Technology, Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv 🇺🇦, Pryazovskyi State Technical University 🇺🇦, and Georgia State University, Perimeter College 🇺🇸 (March 9 – April 18).

📍 A defining feature of the module was the integration of Gerontology and Data Analytics, enabling a meaningful synthesis of humanitarian and technological perspectives. Students not only enhanced their language proficiency but also engaged with disciplinary discourse through the analysis of real-world cases and datasets.

📍 The learning process was conducted in an asynchronous format: participants completed academic writing tasks in English, performed data analysis, and developed data storytelling skills.

📍 Intercultural interaction became a core value of the project. people.about:
What happens when students stop being just learners — and start becoming researchers, creators and leaders?
This is the question that has shaped much of my academic journey.
I am an ESP/EAP lecturer, EFL coach and Academic Lead of COIL Programmes at the Department of Foreign Languages for Mathematical Faculties, Educational and Scientific Institute of Philology, Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, Ukraine.

Since 2019, together with colleagues and international partners, we have been developing international virtual learning experiences connecting students across Ukraine, Great Britain, the UK, the USA, Asia and Europe. My particular focus is on integrating Research-Based Learning (RBL) with EAP and COIL, creating an environment where students do not simply acquire academic and professional skills — they use them to investigate real problems, design their own projects, collaborate internationally and take responsibility for their learning. RBL is especially important for postgraduate students while UGs master Experiential Learning (EL).

I believe they should have opportunities to move beyond the role of students completing assignments and experience themselves as emerging researchers, project designers and academic leaders. Through our interdisciplinary COIL modules, students work across cultural boundaries, develop research and communication skills, and learn from both academic and industry perspectives. At the same time, our team organises webinars, workshops and international academic events supporting students in developing, presenting and preparing their research for publication in peer-reviewed journals.
